decisions.reason: The candidate already permits whisk-position adjustment for splash mitigation. Tuning whisk length and depth does not change its splash-control target or necessarily establish a new mitigation rule.
Whisk length and depth tuning does not change the approved speed range, continuous-operation constraint, or supported operating modes.
The source changes whisk positioning dimensions, not bowl depth, capacity, or refilling policy.
The client identifies mixing consistency and frothing as factors to assess, but the freelancer's tuning commitment does not alter the candidate's existing output-quality requirements.
Tuning the installed whisk's length and operating depth does not change the selected whisk-head design, material, powder suitability, or head-size requirement.
The source concerns whisk positioning and has no effect on placard text, placement, orientation, or display sides.
Mechanical tuning of whisk length and depth does not change electrical loads, power-supply headroom, or cooling requirements.
The source does not change the stainless-steel material requirements for the whisk or spout.
Although whisk geometry can affect clearance, the source does not state that the tuning changes or resolves bowl-removal and swapping behavior.
Adjusting whisk length and operating depth does not change whether the whisk is removable quickly, simply, or without tools.
The source has no effect on support-base graphics, lettering, typography, or logo treatment.
Whisk length and depth tuning does not change the prototype's 120V wall-power requirement or deferred battery-power decision.
